about: Tool-choice steering evaluation (STP-1805, from STP-1476). Each case is a user request with the kind of input it carries (words, data, mixed, lookup, help), the server mode it needs, the tools a model should reach for (use) and must not (avoid), and the steering facts that must be in front of the model for that choice. Cases come in pairs (same pair id) that differ only in their input and so in their route. The evaluation is deterministic, with no model call: a fact is a set of case-insensitive regular expressions that must all match one text - the live server's instructions in a mode, the knowledge server's instructions, or a contract tool's description or edge cases. A case passes when all its facts hold. Facts owned by this repo (owner mcp) must always hold; facts owned by the contract (owner contract) that fail are gaps, each pointing at its proposal in docs/proposals/STP-1805-contract-wording.md, and the floor in test/tool-choice-eval.test.ts rises as the contract adopts them.

code-source.claim: Symbol codes come from data or from STP, never from the model.

words-to-recognition.claim: A symbol described in words goes to recognition (simulated speech plus strokes); STP produces the code.

words-not-addsymbol.claim: AddSymbol is not the tool for a symbol described in words.
patterns: Do not use AddSymbol for it

data-pass-through.claim: Structured data with codes passes through AddSymbol with each code exactly as given.
patterns: AddSymbol with each code exactly as given

data-imports.claim: STP content goes through an import, named when destructive mode lists them.
patterns: an import for STP content \(ImportPlanDataFromObjectSet, ImportCoaFromObjectSet

data-imports-need-destructive.claim: In write mode the imports are not listed; the instructions say how to get them instead of naming them.
patterns: imports are listed in destructive mode, STP_DESTRUCTIVE=1

data-not-rewritten.claim: Data is not re-recognized or rewritten; a rejection is reported with its reason, never patched with an invented code.
patterns: Do not re-recognize or rewrite that data
report the outcome and its reason
rather than substituting a code of your own

mixed-does-both.claim: A mixed request does both, naming existing objects by poid.

lookup-from-stp.claim: A code question is answered by looking it up in STP, saying where it came from.

searchsymbol-templates.claim: SearchSymbol's codes are a symbol type's codes, not a finished symbol to edit.

c-to-d-only.claim: 2525C maps to 2525D, never the reverse; an empty charlieSidc means there is no 2525C code.
patterns: 2525C codes map to 2525D, never the reverse

audience-live.claim: Answers match the asker: outcome for a planner, methods and events for an integrator.
patterns: planning in STP gets the outcome
integrating with STP also gets the methods

audience-integrator.claim: An integrator gets methods, params, events and failure modes, with the source.
patterns: gets the methods, params, events and failure modes

audience-end-user.claim: An end user gets what to say, draw or click, in planning terms, without JSON-RPC.
patterns: what to say, draw or click

knowledge-code-source.claim: Help answers never write out a code the sources do not give.
patterns: do not write out a code the sources do not give
2525C codes map to 2525D, never the reverse

addsymbol-input-source.claim: AddSymbol's description names where the code comes from and says not to compose one.
patterns: user's data, a file or STP

addsymbol-names-recognition.claim: AddSymbol's description points a symbol described in words to SendSimulatedSpeechRecognition.

simspeech-for-words.claim: SendSimulatedSpeechRecognition's description says it is the path for a symbol described in words, with SendInk for its place.

sendink-for-placement.claim: SendInk's description covers placing a described symbol (a point or outline) together with simulated speech.

searchsymbol-bridge-route.claim: SearchSymbol's description names the bridge's /symbol-index.json route as an index source.

searchsymbol-templates-contract.claim: SearchSymbol's description says its codes are a symbol type's codes (templates), not codes to complete by hand.

searchsymbol-edge-source.claim: SearchSymbol's no-index refusal names the source, a path or a URL, not only a path.
patterns: symbol index not available: <(source|path or URL)>

import-objectset-as-given.claim: The object-set import says it takes STP objects as given.
